But in the mornings of these three days he scheduled the work on the major matters—in chunks of ninety minutes each. Another fairly common method is to schedule a daily work period at home in the morning. • One of the most effective executives in Professor Sune Carlson’s study, mentioned above, spent ninety minutes each morning before going to work in a study without telephone at home. Even if this means working very early so as to get to the office on time, it is preferable to the most popular way of getting to the important work: taking it home in the evening and spending three hours after dinner on it.
